original_caption: Figure 3. Adaptive whitelisting provides high fidelity barcode identification and correction. A-C. Characterization of false positive barcode assignment rate. Using three datasets, random, size matched sets of “off-list” barcodes were provided as the whitelist to each tool and the rate at which reads were assigned to this list was assessed (A). Quantification of the of total read count (B) and read depth (C) assigned to false positive barcodes by each tool. Statistical significance determined by one-way ANOVA (****p < 0.0001). D-G. Barcode correction outcomes (D). Using the LongBench dataset, the total read counts (E), the read depth (F), and the percentage of reads per barcode (G) derived from corrected off-list or the two failure modes were quantified for each tool.
new_caption: Figure 3. Adaptive whitelisting provides high fidelity barcode identification and correction. A-C. Characterization of false positive barcode assignment rate. Using three datasets, random, size matched sets of “off-list” barcodes were provided as the whitelist to each tool and the rate at which reads were assigned to this list was assessed (A). Quantification of the of total read count (B) and read depth (C) assigned to false positive barcodes by each tool. Statistical significance determined by one-way ANOVA (****p < 0.0001). D-G. Barcode correction was classified by exact observed source-barcode membership (D). Corrected off-list: a source outside the complete chemistry catalog was changed to a tool-selected target. Failure mode 1: a catalog-valid source outside the Cell Ranger filtered set was changed to a tool-selected target. Failure mode 2: a source in the Cell Ranger filtered set was changed to a different barcode in that set that was also selected by the tool. Counts used unique original-read–target-barcode pairs. Total counts (E), counts per target barcode (F), and class percentages among all such pairs assigned by the same tool to each target (G) were compared across the four LongBench inputs. These classes describe observed barcode changes and reference-set membership; they do not establish cellular origin or correction accuracy.
